chapters.label: The company
chapters.title: Independent engine management from Zug, Switzerland
chapters.body: Flight Hour Solution is an independent jet-engine management consultancy. We work for airlines, lessors, MROs and government operators across seventeen engine and APU models, from the CFM56 to the Honeywell 131-9 APU.
chapters.source: 01-company-profile.md section 1 (registered seat Zug, register entry 26 September 2024) and section 4.2 (client types); 02-website-content-inventory.md section 4 (engine families and models).

chapters.label: The purchase
chapters.title: A shop visit is a multi-million-dollar purchase
chapters.body: An engine needs three to five shop visits in its life. A performance restoration typically costs several million US dollars. We treat each as a purchase.
tags: 3 to 5 shop visits per engine life
chapters.source: 06-market-context-and-seo.md section 1.2: MTU, an engine typically needs 3 to 5 shop visits over its life [F]; Magnetic Group, CFM56 repair costs +50 to 75% since 2019 [F]; the phrase 'typically several million US dollars per visit' is the wording 06 section 1.2 permits. Section 1.3: Bain, turnaround times +35% for legacy and +150% for new-generation engines against pre-pandemic [F].

chapters.label: The workscope
chapters.title: Workscope discipline protects value on both sides
chapters.body: Reserve clauses and redelivery conditions are the lease terms most likely to end in a dispute. We set each workscope against the lease, the LLP plan and the records.
chapters.source: 06-market-context-and-seo.md section 1.7: Acumen, maintenance-reserve clauses and redelivery conditions are the two lease provisions most likely to trigger multi-million-dollar end-of-lease disputes; disputes centre on LLP valuations, deferred defects, incomplete back-to-birth records and fair wear and tear [F]. Deliverables: 02 section 4.

chapters.label: The evidence
chapters.title: An independent read of the data and records
chapters.body: We give a second opinion on ECM and EHM trends, borescope video and test-cell results. Records get the same scrutiny, back to birth.

situations.title: Three situations we are hired for

items.title: A shop visit is coming
items.text: An engine is coming off wing and the shop's workscope, quote or invoice needs an independent check. We manage the visit from induction planning to redelivery.

items.title: A lease is ending or an engine is changing hands
items.text: Redelivery conditions, maintenance reserves, LLP status and back-to-birth records decide what the transition costs. We work for the lessee or the lessor.

items.title: You need an engine, or need to sell one
items.text: Through our Assets line we source and market engines and aircraft. Every brokered asset is declared as such and kept apart from advisory work.

situations.source: 07-recommendations-and-brief.md section 5 (Home brief: shop visit, lease transition, sourcing) and section 2.3 (Advisory and Assets lines); 01 section 4.3 (LinkedIn: sourcing, technical advisory and engine sales support).

services.title: What we do
services.intro: Eight services, each with its deliverables listed on its own page. Most engagements start with the workscope.

rows.title: Shop visit management
rows.text: Full or overview management of an engine shop visit, from pre-induction to redelivery, with every workscope line, finding and invoice item checked independently.

rows.title: Workscope and removal planning
rows.text: Removal timing, workscope compilation and maintenance cost forecasting for the fleet, so each engine comes off wing at the right time with the right workscope.

rows.title: Lease return and asset management
rows.text: Redelivery support for lessee or lessor, maintenance reserve calculations and claim analysis, and records audits back to birth, through the lease and at its end.

rows.title: Contracts, MRO and supply chain
rows.text: Engine overhaul, repair, purchase and lease contract negotiation, warranty management, invoice review and material sourcing support, on your side of the table.

rows.title: Predictive maintenance and analytics
rows.text: An independent read of your ECM and EHM data, borescope video and test results: when to watch, when to pull, what the shop should find.

rows.title: Technical due diligence
rows.text: Engine evaluation and selection, records audits back to birth, maintenance forecasts and teardown valuations for buyers, lessors, lenders and investors.

rows.title: Military and government programmes
rows.text: Shop visit management, maintenance forecasting, contract negotiation and post-repair evaluation for governmental and military operators, with the OEM or a single depot on the other side of the table.

rows.title: Training and knowledge transfer
rows.text: Practical training for powerplant, procurement and asset teams on shop visits, workscopes, invoices and lease returns, built from the methods we use on engagements.

services.source: 02-website-content-inventory.md section 4 (service taxonomy, verbatim deliverables); 01-company-profile.md section 1 (registered purpose includes training and knowledge transfer) and section 4.2 (Swiss Aerospace Cluster core competences).

process.title: How a managed shop visit works
process.intro: Five steps. Every decision is recorded against the workscope so the invoice, the records and the lease agree at the end.

steps.title: Induction planning
steps.text: Removal reason and technical status reviewed, records and LLP status checked, slot and transport confirmed. A preliminary workscope is drafted against the lease and the planning guide before the engine reaches the shop.

steps.title: Workscope
steps.text: The shop's proposed workscope is compared line by line with the planning guide, the lease conditions and the LLP stub lives. Only what the engine needs is agreed, in writing, before disassembly.

steps.title: Table inspection
steps.text: Attended in person once the engine is stripped. Each finding is photographed and recorded, repair or replace is decided part by part, and scrap is reviewed for material value.

steps.title: Repair approvals and invoice review
steps.text: Repair quotes and material choices, new or used serviceable, are approved against the agreed workscope. The invoice is then reconciled against that workscope and the recorded findings before it is paid.

steps.title: Test cell and redelivery
steps.text: Test-cell results are reviewed against the acceptance limits, the post-shop-visit documentation is audited and warranty items are logged. The engine is redelivered with a records pack ready for the next lease or transition.

process.source: Steps and deliverables: 02-website-content-inventory.md section 4 (Shop Visit Management: workscope compilation and review, dirty condition and table inspection, test cell overview, invoice review, scrap review and material value extraction, post-shop visit documentation audit, warranty management); 06 section 1.7 (what shop visit management is expected to contain); 05 section 6 (managed shop visit timeline pattern).

independence.title: Not owned by an MRO, lessor or OEM
independence.text: Flight Hour Solution is owned by its managing director, not by an MRO, a lessor or an engine manufacturer. On advisory work we act for the client alone. closing.headline: Send us the workscope before you sign it
closing.sub: Tell us the engine, the shop and the date. We will tell you where an independent review earns its fee.

faq.q: What does shop visit management include?
faq.a: Induction planning, workscope compilation and review, attendance at the table inspection, borescope and test-cell overview, repair and material approvals, invoice review, scrap review and a post-shop-visit documentation audit. It can be run as full management or as an overview of a visit your own team runs.

faq.q: Is Flight Hour Solution independent of MROs, lessors and engine manufacturers?
faq.a: Yes. The company is owned by its managing director and is not owned by an MRO, a lessor or an OEM. When it sources or brokers an engine or aircraft, that is declared and kept separate from advisory work.

faq.q: Which engine families do you cover?
faq.a: CFM56-3, -5 and -7; LEAP-1A, -1B and -1C; V2500-A1, -A5 and -D5; PW4000-94, -100 and -112; Honeywell APU 131-9A, -9B and -9D; and the TPE331, T76 and TFE731.

faq.q: When should we involve you in a shop visit?
faq.a: Before the workscope is agreed with the shop, ideally at removal planning. We can also join at the table inspection or at the invoice stage, but the largest decisions are made in the workscope.

From Zug, Switzerland, and on site wherever the engine is: at the shop for table inspections, at the test cell and at redelivery. Clients are airlines, lessors, MROs and government operators worldwide.
